title: Breach of contract
settingKo: 납품 업체가 계약을 어겨 변호사와 대응 방안을 상담합니다.

lines.text: Our supplier missed three delivery dates in a row, and we lost a major customer as a result.
lines.ko: 공급 업체가 납기를 세 번 연속 어겨서 그 결과 주요 고객을 잃었어요.

lines.text: Does the contract specify delivery dates, and is there a liquidated damages clause?
lines.ko: 계약서에 납기가 명시돼 있나요? 그리고 손해배상액 예정 조항이 있나요?

lines.text: Yes to both. It says two percent of the order value for each week of delay, capped at ten percent.
lines.ko: 둘 다 있어요. 지연 1주당 주문 금액의 2퍼센트, 최대 10퍼센트라고 돼 있어요.

lines.text: Then we start by sending a formal notice of breach and claiming the agreed damages before considering anything further.
lines.ko: 그럼 다른 걸 고려하기 전에 공식 위반 통지서를 보내고 약정된 손해배상을 청구하는 것부터 시작하죠.

options: 공식 위반 통지와 약정 손해배상 청구

phrases.en: Is there a liquidated damages clause?

response.situationKo: 거래처가 계약을 어겼습니다. 변호사에게 상황을 정확히 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Walk me through what happened and what the contract says.

answers.text: Under the contract, they were obliged to deliver by the fifteenth, but they failed to deliver until the thirtieth.
Clause nine sets out the delivery schedule, and as a result of the delay, we've incurred about forty thousand in losses.
They missed the deadline twice, didn't notify us, and our client cancelled because of it.
Short version: they didn't deliver, we lost a client, and the contract has a penalty clause.

title: Before you sign the NDA
settingKo: 협업 전 상대 회사의 비밀유지계약서를 사내 변호사와 검토합니다.

lines.text: This NDA is mutual in name only. Their obligations last two years, but ours last indefinitely.
lines.ko: 이 NDA는 이름만 상호적이에요. 상대 의무는 2년인데 우리 의무는 무기한이에요.

lines.text: Is that unusual, or just aggressive drafting?
lines.ko: 그게 이례적인 건가요, 아니면 그냥 공격적으로 쓴 건가요?

lines.text: Aggressive. I'd also narrow the definition of confidential information, which currently covers almost anything we say in a meeting.
lines.ko: 공격적인 거예요. 기밀 정보 정의도 좁히겠어요. 지금은 회의에서 하는 거의 모든 말이 포함돼요.

lines.text: Let's propose equal terms of three years and limit it to information marked confidential in writing.
lines.ko: 양측 동일하게 3년으로 하고, 서면으로 기밀 표시된 정보로 한정하자고 제안하죠.

phrases.en: Narrow the definition of confidential information.

response.situationKo: 상대가 불리한 계약 조항을 고치지 않으려 합니다. 수정 요청을 논리적으로 해 보세요.
response.prompt: That's our standard NDA. We don't usually make changes.

answers.text: We understand. However, for a mutual agreement, we'd propose reciprocal terms on duration.
Two small changes would make it reasonable for both sides: equal duration and a narrower definition.
An indefinite obligation isn't industry standard. Three years is what we typically see.
Totally get it, but we can't sign something one-sided. Can we meet halfway?

title: Someone copied our name
settingKo: 경쟁사가 비슷한 브랜드명을 쓰기 시작해 지식재산권 변호사와 상의합니다.

lines.text: A new company is selling almost identical products under the name Bloomly, and our brand is Bloomlee.
lines.ko: 새 회사가 블루밀리라는 이름으로 거의 똑같은 제품을 파는데 우리 브랜드는 블루밀리(Bloomlee)예요.

lines.text: Is your trademark registered in the categories where they're selling?
lines.ko: 그 회사가 파는 분야에 귀사 상표가 등록돼 있나요?

lines.text: Yes, for skincare and cosmetics, since twenty twenty-two.
lines.ko: 네, 2022년부터 스킨케어와 화장품 분야로요.

lines.text: Then there's a strong likelihood of confusion. We'll start with a cease-and-desist letter and collect evidence of customers mixing you up.
lines.ko: 그럼 혼동 가능성이 높아요. 침해 중지 요구서부터 보내고, 고객이 혼동한 증거를 모으죠.

response.situationKo: 변호사가 고객 혼동의 증거를 묻습니다. 구체적인 사례를 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you have any evidence that customers are actually confused?

answers.text: Yes, we've received about a dozen complaints about products we never sold.
answers.noteKo: 판 적 없는 제품에 대한 불만은 강한 증거예요.

answers.text: For example, several customers tagged us in reviews of their product by mistake.
We have screenshots of people asking whether the two brands are the same company.
Tons. Our support inbox is full of returns for things we don't even make.

title: Can they fire me for that?
settingKo: 갑자기 해고 통보를 받은 직원이 노동법 변호사와 상담합니다.

lines.text: They dismissed me two weeks after I reported a safety issue. They're calling it restructuring.
lines.ko: 안전 문제를 신고하고 2주 뒤에 해고됐어요. 회사는 구조 조정이라고 해요.

lines.text: The timing is significant. Was anyone else let go in this so-called restructuring?
lines.ko: 시점이 중요해요. 이른바 구조 조정에서 다른 사람도 해고됐나요?

lines.text: No, just me, and they've already posted a job ad for my role.
lines.ko: 아니요, 저만요. 그리고 벌써 제 자리 채용 공고를 냈어요.

lines.text: That undermines their explanation considerably. Keep every email and the job posting. This could be a retaliation claim.
lines.ko: 그건 회사 해명을 크게 약화시켜요. 모든 메일과 채용 공고를 보관하세요. 보복 해고 소송이 될 수 있어요.

options: 본인만 해고되고 같은 자리 채용 공고를 냈다

phrases.en: This could be a retaliation claim.
phrases.ko: 보복 해고 소송이 될 수 있어요.

response.situationKo: 변호사가 사건을 시간 순서대로 설명해 달라고 합니다.
response.prompt: Give me a timeline of events, starting with the report.

answers.text: On March third, I reported the broken guardrail in writing. Two weeks later, I was told my role was being eliminated.
I emailed my manager about the issue, then the following Monday my access was suddenly restricted.
First the report, then a sudden bad review, then the dismissal letter. All within a month.
Basically, I spoke up, they went quiet, and two weeks later I was out.

title: Small claims court
settingKo: 소액 재판에서 판사 앞에 자신의 주장을 간단히 진술합니다.

lines.text: You're claiming twelve hundred dollars from the contractor. In your own words, what happened?
lines.ko: 시공업자에게 1,200달러를 청구하셨네요. 직접 무슨 일이 있었는지 말씀해 보세요.

lines.text: I paid in full upfront for a new fence, but he only installed half of it and stopped answering my calls.
lines.ko: 새 울타리 비용을 전액 선불로 냈는데 절반만 설치하고 전화를 안 받아요.

lines.text: Do you have documentation of the payment and the agreed scope of work?
lines.ko: 결제 기록과 합의한 작업 범위에 대한 서류가 있나요?

lines.text: Yes, the signed quote, my bank transfer, and photos of the unfinished fence with dates.
lines.ko: 네, 서명한 견적서, 계좌 이체 내역, 날짜가 찍힌 미완성 울타리 사진이 있어요.

response.situationKo: 판사가 원하는 결과를 묻습니다. 명확하게 요구해 보세요.
response.prompt: And what outcome are you asking the court for?

answers.text: I'm asking for a refund of six hundred dollars for the work that wasn't completed, plus court costs.
Either he finishes the fence within thirty days, or he refunds the unfinished portion.
Repayment for the half he didn't build. That's all I want.
Honestly, just my money back for what wasn't done, Your Honor.

title: Commercial lease terms
settingKo: 카페 창업 전 상가 임대차 계약서의 조항을 부동산 변호사와 검토합니다.

lines.text: The rent looks fair, but this clause makes you responsible for all structural repairs, including the roof.
lines.ko: 임대료는 적정한데 이 조항은 지붕을 포함한 모든 구조 수리를 임차인 책임으로 해요.

lines.text: That sounds expensive. Isn't the roof normally the landlord's responsibility?
lines.ko: 돈이 많이 들 것 같네요. 지붕은 보통 임대인 책임 아닌가요?

lines.text: Usually, yes. I'd also push for a rent-free fit-out period, since you'll need three months to renovate.
lines.ko: 보통은 그렇죠. 인테리어에 석 달이 필요하니 무상 공사 기간도 요구하겠어요.

lines.text: And can we add a break clause, in case the café doesn't work out after two years?
lines.ko: 그리고 2년 후 카페가 잘 안 될 경우를 대비해 중도 해지 조항을 넣을 수 있을까요?

response.situationKo: 임대인이 조건 변경을 꺼립니다. 합리적인 근거로 설득해 보세요.
response.prompt: The landlord says every tenant signs these exact terms.

answers.text: That may be, but given that we're signing for ten years, we'd expect the roof to stay with the owner.
In exchange for the break clause, we'd be willing to pay a slightly higher deposit.
We're a long-term tenant who'll improve the property. That should count for something.
Every tenant? Then let's be the first to ask nicely.

title: In the emergency room
settingKo: 응급실 간호사가 환자의 증상을 빠르게 파악합니다.

lines.text: On a scale of one to ten, how bad is the chest pain, and does it spread anywhere?
lines.ko: 1에서 10 중 가슴 통증이 얼마나 심하고, 다른 곳으로 퍼지나요?

lines.text: About a seven. It goes into my left arm, and I feel short of breath.
lines.ko: 7 정도요. 왼팔로 퍼지고 숨이 차요.

lines.text: Any history of heart problems, and are you on any blood thinners?
lines.ko: 심장 질환 병력이 있거나 혈액 희석제를 드시나요?

lines.text: We're going to do an ECG right away and take some blood. A doctor will see you in a few minutes.
lines.ko: 바로 심전도를 찍고 피를 뽑을게요. 의사가 몇 분 안에 볼 거예요.

response.situationKo: 응급실에서 증상을 정확하고 빠르게 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: What brings you in today?

answers.text: A sharp pain in my lower right abdomen. It started about six hours ago and it's getting worse.
answers.noteKo: 위치, 성격, 시작 시점, 변화를 말해요.

answers.text: I fell off my bike, and my wrist is swollen. It's worse when I try to move it.
A terrible headache since this morning, and the light is really bothering my eyes.
My daughter has a fever of thirty-nine point five and she's been vomiting since lunch.

title: Informed consent
settingKo: 외과의가 수술 전 환자에게 위험과 대안을 설명합니다.

lines.text: The procedure is keyhole surgery to remove your gallbladder. Most patients go home the same day.
lines.ko: 복강경으로 쓸개를 제거하는 수술이에요. 대부분 당일 퇴원해요.

lines.text: The main risks are bleeding, infection, and, rarely, injury to the bile duct, which happens in fewer than one in five hundred cases.
lines.ko: 주요 위험은 출혈, 감염, 드물게 담관 손상이 있는데 500건 중 1건 미만이에요.

lines.text: What happens if I decide not to have the operation?
lines.ko: 수술을 안 받기로 하면 어떻게 되나요?

lines.text: The attacks would likely continue and could lead to inflammation of the pancreas, which is far more serious.
lines.ko: 발작이 계속될 가능성이 높고 훨씬 심각한 췌장염으로 이어질 수 있어요.

gist.questionKo: 수술을 안 받으면 생길 수 있는 문제는?

phrases.en: Most patients go home the same day.
Fewer than one in five hundred cases.

response.situationKo: 수술 전 의사에게 꼭 확인해야 할 질문을 해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you have any questions before you sign the consent form?

answers.text: How many of these procedures have you performed, and what's your complication rate?
How long is the recovery before I can go back to work?
What are the alternatives, and why do you recommend surgery over them?
Will I be fully asleep, or is it local anesthesia?

title: Drug interactions
settingKo: 약사가 새 처방약과 기존 약의 상호작용을 확인합니다.

lines.text: Before I fill this antibiotic, are you taking anything else, including supplements or herbal remedies?
lines.ko: 이 항생제를 조제하기 전에 영양제나 한약을 포함해 다른 걸 드시고 계세요?

lines.text: I take a statin for cholesterol, and St. John's wort for my mood.
lines.ko: 콜레스테롤 때문에 스타틴을, 기분 때문에 세인트존스워트를 먹어요.

lines.text: St. John's wort can reduce the effectiveness of several medications, so I'll check with your doctor.
lines.ko: 세인트존스워트는 여러 약의 효과를 떨어뜨릴 수 있어서 의사에게 확인해 볼게요.

lines.text: Also, this antibiotic shouldn't be taken with dairy, so leave two hours between it and any milk.
lines.ko: 그리고 이 항생제는 유제품과 함께 드시면 안 되니 우유와 두 시간 간격을 두세요.

response.situationKo: 약사에게 새 약에 대해 꼭 물어야 할 것을 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Here's your prescription. Any questions?

answers.text: Should I take it with food, and what should I do if I miss a dose?
answers.noteKo: 복용 방법과 누락 시 대처를 물어요.

answers.text: Is it safe to drink alcohol while I'm on this?
answers.noteKo: while I'm on this는 복용 중이에요.

answers.text: Which side effects mean I should stop and call the doctor?
How long until I start feeling better?

title: A first therapy session
settingKo: 심리 상담사가 첫 면담에서 내담자의 상태를 파악합니다.

lines.text: What made you decide to reach out now, rather than six months ago?
lines.ko: 6개월 전이 아니라 왜 지금 연락하기로 하셨어요?

lines.text: I've stopped enjoying things I used to love, and I'm sleeping either too little or far too much.
lines.ko: 좋아하던 걸 더 이상 즐기지 못하고, 잠을 너무 적게 자거나 너무 많이 자요.

lines.text: Thank you for telling me. How long has it been like this, and has it affected your work?
lines.ko: 말씀해 주셔서 고마워요. 그런 지 얼마나 됐고 일에도 영향이 있었나요?

lines.text: About two months. I've been calling in sick more, which isn't like me at all.
lines.ko: 두 달쯤이요. 병가를 더 자주 내고 있는데 전혀 저답지 않아요.

phrases.en: What made you decide to reach out now?
That isn't like me at all.

response.situationKo: 상담사에게 최근 상태를 솔직하게 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: How have you been feeling over the past few weeks?

answers.text: I've been feeling flat most days, and I find it hard to concentrate at work.
Lately I feel anxious in the mornings, and it's affecting how I sleep.
Honestly, I'm exhausted, even when I haven't done much.
Better than last month, but I still have days where I can't get out of bed.

title: A child with a fever
settingKo: 소아과 의사가 열이 나는 아이의 부모에게 설명합니다.

lines.text: Her temperature has been around thirty-nine for two days, and she's barely eating.
lines.ko: 이틀째 열이 39도 정도이고 거의 안 먹어요.

lines.text: Is she still drinking fluids, and how many wet diapers has she had today?
lines.ko: 수분은 계속 마시나요? 오늘 젖은 기저귀는 몇 개였어요?

lines.text: She drinks a little water, and maybe three wet diapers since this morning.
lines.ko: 물은 조금 마시고 아침부터 젖은 기저귀는 세 개쯤이요.

lines.text: Her ears are inflamed, so it's likely an ear infection. If she stops drinking or becomes very drowsy, come back immediately.
lines.ko: 귀에 염증이 있어서 중이염 같아요. 물을 안 마시거나 많이 처지면 바로 다시 오세요.

phrases.en: If she becomes very drowsy, come back immediately.

response.situationKo: 의사에게 아이의 상태를 정확히 설명하고 걱정을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Tell me what's been going on with your son.

answers.text: Since Tuesday his temperature has been up and down, and today he developed a rash on his chest.
He's been coughing all night and he hasn't kept any food down.
answers.noteKo: kept food down은 토하지 않고 먹다예요.

answers.text: I'm worried because he's unusually quiet and won't play at all.
He's had a fever for three days and keeps pulling at his ear.

title: Rehab after knee surgery
settingKo: 물리치료사가 무릎 수술 후 재활 일정을 설명합니다.

lines.text: For the first two weeks, the goal is reducing swelling and getting your knee fully straight.
lines.ko: 처음 2주는 붓기를 줄이고 무릎을 완전히 펴는 게 목표예요.

lines.text: When can I start running again? I had a half marathon planned.
lines.ko: 언제부터 다시 달릴 수 있어요? 하프 마라톤을 계획했었거든요.

lines.text: Realistically, light jogging at around four months, if your strength tests are at least ninety percent of the other leg.
lines.ko: 현실적으로 넉 달쯤 가볍게 뛸 수 있어요. 근력 검사가 반대쪽 다리의 90퍼센트 이상이라면요.

lines.text: So the race is out, but next spring might be possible.
lines.ko: 그럼 그 대회는 안 되고 내년 봄은 가능할 수도 있겠네요.

response.situationKo: 물리치료사에게 회복 목표와 일정에 대해 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Any questions about the rehab plan?

answers.text: How often should I do these exercises at home, and how much pain is normal?
What should I avoid completely for the next month?
Is it normal for it to swell again in the evening?
When can I drive again? That's my biggest worry, honestly.

title: Fixed or variable?
settingKo: 은행 대출 상담사와 고정 금리와 변동 금리를 비교합니다.

lines.text: The five-year fixed rate is four point two percent, while the variable is currently three point eight.
lines.ko: 5년 고정 금리는 4.2퍼센트이고 변동 금리는 현재 3.8퍼센트예요.

lines.text: The variable is cheaper now, but what happens if rates go up next year?
lines.ko: 지금은 변동이 싸지만 내년에 금리가 오르면 어떻게 되나요?

lines.text: Your monthly payment would rise. A one-point increase would add roughly two hundred dollars a month on this loan.
lines.ko: 월 상환액이 올라가요. 1퍼센트포인트 오르면 이 대출에선 한 달에 대략 200달러가 늘어요.

lines.text: Our budget is already tight, so I think the certainty of a fixed rate is worth the extra cost.
lines.ko: 예산이 이미 빠듯해서 고정 금리의 확실성이 추가 비용만큼 가치 있을 것 같아요.

options: 고정 금리, 예산이 빠듯해 확실성이 필요해서

phrases.en: What happens if rates go up?
The certainty is worth the extra cost.

response.situationKo: 대출 상담사에게 숨은 비용이 없는지 꼼꼼히 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Is there anything else you'd like to know about the loan?

answers.text: Are there any fees for early repayment if we want to pay it off faster?
What's the total cost of the loan over the full term, including all fees?
answers.noteKo: over the term은 대출 기간 전체예요.

answers.text: Is there an arrangement fee, and can it be added to the loan?
What happens when the five years end? Does it jump to a higher rate?

title: The earnings call
settingKo: 분기 실적 발표 후 애널리스트가 CFO에게 질문합니다.

lines.text: Revenue beat expectations, but gross margin fell two points. What's driving the compression?
lines.ko: 매출은 예상을 웃돌았는데 매출총이익률이 2포인트 떨어졌어요. 하락 요인이 뭔가요?

lines.text: Mainly higher shipping costs and a one-off inventory write-down in our European business.
lines.ko: 주로 운송비 상승과 유럽 사업의 일회성 재고 평가 손실 때문이에요.

lines.text: Should we expect that to persist into the next quarter?
lines.ko: 다음 분기에도 그게 지속될 거라고 봐야 하나요?

lines.text: The write-down won't recur, and we've renegotiated freight contracts, so we expect margins to recover by year-end.
lines.ko: 평가 손실은 반복되지 않고 운송 계약을 재협상했으니 연말까지 마진이 회복될 걸로 봅니다.

response.situationKo: 실적 발표에서 날카로운 질문을 받습니다. 원인과 전망을 명확히 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why did customer acquisition costs rise so sharply this quarter?

answers.text: Primarily because we deliberately invested in two new markets, where early costs are always higher.
Part of it was a one-time campaign. We expect costs to normalize within two quarters.
Ad prices rose across the industry, but our retention improved, so lifetime value more than offsets it.
Short answer: we spent ahead of growth on purpose, and early signs say it's paying off.
answers.noteKo: spend ahead of growth는 성장보다 먼저 투자하다예요.

title: Audit findings
settingKo: 외부 감사인이 감사 결과를 회사 재무팀에 설명합니다.

lines.text: We found no material misstatements, but there's a control weakness in how expense claims are approved.
lines.ko: 중요한 왜곡 표시는 없었지만 경비 청구 승인 방식에 내부 통제 약점이 있어요.

lines.text: Can you be more specific about the weakness?
lines.ko: 그 약점을 좀 더 구체적으로 말씀해 주시겠어요?

lines.text: Managers can approve their own team's claims without any second review, even above five thousand dollars.
lines.ko: 관리자가 5천 달러가 넘어도 2차 검토 없이 자기 팀의 청구를 승인할 수 있어요.

lines.text: Understood. We'll introduce a second approver for anything over a thousand and report back next quarter.
lines.ko: 알겠습니다. 천 달러 이상은 2차 승인자를 두고 다음 분기에 보고하겠습니다.

response.situationKo: 감사 지적 사항에 대해 개선 계획을 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: How do you plan to address this finding?

answers.text: We'll implement a second-approver rule above a thousand dollars, effective next month.
Going forward, we'll separate approval from payment so no one controls both steps.
We'll lower the threshold and run a monthly sample check, and we'll report results to the audit committee.
Fair catch. We'll fix the workflow in the system so it physically can't be skipped.

title: Talking to an accountant
settingKo: 프리랜서가 세무사와 경비 처리에 대해 상담합니다.

lines.text: I work from home three days a week. Can I deduct part of my rent and utilities?
lines.ko: 주 3일 재택근무를 하는데 월세와 공과금 일부를 공제할 수 있나요?

lines.text: Yes, but only the portion used exclusively for work, usually calculated by floor space.
lines.ko: 네, 하지만 업무 전용으로 쓰는 부분만이고 보통 면적으로 계산해요.

lines.text: My desk is in the corner of the living room, not a separate office.
lines.ko: 제 책상은 거실 구석에 있고 따로 사무실은 아니에요.

lines.text: Then it's harder to justify. A dedicated room would make the claim much stronger if you're ever audited.
lines.ko: 그럼 정당화하기 어려워요. 전용 방이 있으면 세무 조사 시 훨씬 유리해요.

phrases.en: The portion used exclusively for work.

response.situationKo: 세무사에게 공제 가능한 비용을 확인해 보세요.
response.prompt: What expenses are you hoping to claim this year?

answers.text: Can I claim my new laptop and design software subscriptions?
Is travel to client meetings deductible, and what records do I need to keep?
I have receipts for a training course. Does that count as a business expense?
Honestly, I have a shoebox of receipts. Where do I even start?

title: Why are we over budget?
settingKo: 재무 담당자가 부서장에게 예산 초과 원인을 묻습니다.

lines.text: Your department is eighteen percent over budget year to date. Can you walk me through the variance?
lines.ko: 부서가 연초 대비 18퍼센트 예산 초과예요. 차이를 설명해 주시겠어요?

lines.text: Most of it is contractor spend. We lost two engineers in March and had to backfill with contractors at a higher rate.
lines.ko: 대부분 외주 비용이에요. 3월에 엔지니어 두 명이 나가서 더 비싼 외주로 메웠어요.

lines.text: Is that temporary, or should we reforecast for the rest of the year?
lines.ko: 일시적인가요, 아니면 남은 해를 다시 전망해야 하나요?

lines.text: Both hires start next month, so contractor costs should drop sharply from August onwards.
lines.ko: 두 명 모두 다음 달 입사라서 8월부터 외주 비용이 크게 줄 거예요.

response.situationKo: 예산이 초과된 이유를 재무팀에 설명하고 대책을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Marketing is twenty percent over plan. What happened?
keywords: for the rest of the year

answers.text: The main driver was an unplanned trade show. We've since cut two smaller campaigns to offset it.
Ad prices spiked in Q2. For the rest of the year, we're shifting budget to cheaper channels.
We pulled spend forward for the launch, so we expect to come in on budget by December.
Honestly, we got ambitious. Here's the plan to claw it back.

title: Dilution and the cap table
settingKo: 창업자가 투자 후 지분 희석에 대해 변호사와 이야기합니다.

lines.text: After this round and the new option pool, your stake goes from sixty percent to about forty-two.
lines.ko: 이번 라운드와 새 스톡옵션 풀 이후 지분이 60퍼센트에서 약 42퍼센트로 줄어요.

lines.text: That's a bigger drop than I expected. Why does the option pool come out of our share?
lines.ko: 예상보다 많이 줄었네요. 왜 옵션 풀이 우리 몫에서 나가죠?

lines.text: Investors usually require the pool to be created before their money comes in, so it dilutes existing holders only.
lines.ko: 투자자는 보통 투자금이 들어오기 전에 풀을 만들라고 해서 기존 주주만 희석돼요.

lines.text: Then let's push for a smaller pool, sized for the hires we actually plan over eighteen months.
lines.ko: 그럼 실제로 18개월간 계획한 채용에 맞춰 풀을 더 작게 하자고 요구하죠.

options: 실제 채용 계획에 맞춰 풀을 줄이자고 요구

phrases.en: Sized for the hires we actually plan.

response.situationKo: 투자 조건 중 불리한 부분을 협상해 보세요.
response.prompt: The investors want a twenty percent option pool before the round.

answers.text: Based on our hiring plan, ten percent covers everyone through next year. We'd propose that instead.
Could we create the pool post-money, so the dilution is shared?
Twenty is hard to justify. Fifteen with a top-up option later?
That's a lot of our company for people we haven't hired yet. Let's talk numbers.

title: Code review
settingKo: 시니어 개발자가 주니어의 코드에 리뷰를 남깁니다.

lines.text: The logic works, but this function is doing three things at once: fetching, validating, and saving.
lines.ko: 로직은 동작하는데 이 함수가 세 가지를 한꺼번에 해요. 가져오기, 검증, 저장이요.

lines.text: Should I split it into separate functions?
lines.ko: 별도 함수로 나눌까요?

lines.text: Yes, it'll make testing much easier. Also, this query runs inside a loop, which will be slow with large datasets.
lines.ko: 네, 테스트가 훨씬 쉬워질 거예요. 그리고 이 쿼리가 반복문 안에서 돌아서 데이터가 많으면 느려질 거예요.

lines.text: Got it. I'll batch the query and add unit tests for each piece before you take another look.
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 쿼리를 일괄 처리로 바꾸고 각 부분에 단위 테스트를 추가한 뒤 다시 보여 드릴게요.

phrases.en: This function is doing three things at once.
phrases.ko: 이 함수가 세 가지를 한꺼번에 해요.

response.situationKo: 동료 코드에 리뷰를 남겨야 합니다. 건설적으로 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Could you review my pull request when you get a chance?

answers.text: Nice work overall. One suggestion: consider handling the empty-list edge case explicitly.
Looks good. Just a nit: the variable name 'data2' could be more descriptive.
Could we move the config values out of the code and into environment variables?
Approved with small comments! Ping me if anything's unclear.

title: Designing for scale
settingKo: 아키텍트들이 트래픽 급증에 대비한 설계를 논의합니다.

lines.text: During the sale, traffic will spike to roughly ten times normal. Our database is already the bottleneck.
lines.ko: 세일 기간엔 트래픽이 평소의 약 10배로 치솟아요. 데이터베이스가 이미 병목이에요.

lines.text: Most of those requests are product page views, so a cache in front of the database would absorb the bulk of it.
lines.ko: 대부분 상품 페이지 조회라서 데이터베이스 앞에 캐시를 두면 대부분을 흡수할 거예요.

lines.text: What about stock levels? If the cache is stale, we could oversell.
lines.ko: 재고는요? 캐시가 오래된 값이면 초과 판매할 수 있어요.

lines.text: Then we cache the page but check stock directly against the database at checkout.
lines.ko: 그럼 페이지는 캐시하고 재고는 결제 시점에 데이터베이스에서 직접 확인하죠.

options: 결제 시 재고를 DB에서 직접 확인

response.situationKo: 설계 회의에서 대안의 장단점을 비교해 의견을 내 보세요.
response.prompt: Should we split the monolith into microservices before the launch?

answers.text: The trade-off is speed now versus flexibility later. Before a launch, I'd keep the monolith and extract only the checkout service.
In the short term, microservices add operational complexity we don't have time to manage.
I'd suggest we measure first. If one module is the bottleneck, scale that, not everything.
Risky timing. Let's ship, then refactor once things calm down.

title: A phishing incident
settingKo: 직원이 피싱 링크를 클릭해 보안팀이 대응합니다.

lines.text: I clicked a link in an email that looked like it was from IT, and I entered my password.
lines.ko: IT팀에서 온 것 같은 메일의 링크를 눌러서 비밀번호를 입력했어요.

lines.text: Thanks for reporting it quickly. That makes a huge difference. When did this happen?
lines.ko: 빨리 신고해 줘서 고마워요. 그게 큰 차이를 만들어요. 언제 그랬어요?

lines.text: About ten minutes ago. I realized something was off when the page didn't load properly.
lines.ko: 10분쯤 전이요. 페이지가 제대로 안 열려서 뭔가 이상하다는 걸 알았어요.

lines.text: We're resetting your password and signing you out of every device now. Then we'll check for any unusual logins.
lines.ko: 지금 비밀번호를 초기화하고 모든 기기에서 로그아웃시킬게요. 그다음 비정상 로그인을 확인할 거예요.

response.situationKo: 보안팀에 의심스러운 메일을 신고해 보세요.
response.prompt: Security team, what's up?

answers.text: I received a suspicious email asking me to verify my payroll details. I didn't click anything.
The sender address looks almost like our CEO's, but one letter is different. Should I forward it to you?
I think I just got phished. It asked for my login and I typed it in before I noticed.
Weird invoice email with an attachment from a vendor we don't use. Want a look?

title: Writing the product spec
settingKo: 프로덕트 매니저와 엔지니어가 새 기능 명세를 다듬습니다.

lines.text: The goal is to let users schedule posts in advance. What's unclear from an engineering point of view?
lines.ko: 목표는 사용자가 게시물을 미리 예약하게 하는 거예요. 엔지니어링 관점에서 불분명한 게 있나요?

lines.text: Time zones, mostly. If a user travels, should the post follow their new location or the original one?
lines.ko: 주로 시간대요. 사용자가 여행하면 새 위치를 따라야 해요, 원래 위치를 따라야 해요?

lines.text: Good catch. Let's keep the time zone fixed to when they scheduled it, and show it clearly in the interface.
lines.ko: 잘 짚었어요. 예약할 때의 시간대로 고정하고 화면에 명확히 보여 주죠.

lines.text: And what's out of scope for version one? Editing a scheduled post, for example?
lines.ko: 그리고 1버전에서 제외할 건요? 예를 들어 예약된 게시물 수정은요?

phrases.en: What's out of scope for version one?

response.situationKo: 명세서의 불분명한 부분을 PM에게 질문해 보세요.
response.prompt: Does the spec make sense? Anything missing?

answers.text: What happens if the user deletes their account while a post is still scheduled?
Could you clarify the success metric? Is it adoption, or the number of posts scheduled?
How should we handle failures, for example if the platform is down at the scheduled time?
Mostly clear! Just need to know what's explicitly out of scope so we don't overbuild.

title: Data privacy request
settingKo: 개인정보 담당자가 사용자의 데이터 삭제 요청 처리를 논의합니다.

lines.text: We received a request from a user in Germany to delete all of their personal data.
lines.ko: 독일 사용자에게서 개인정보를 모두 삭제해 달라는 요청을 받았어요.

lines.text: We have one month to respond. Is their data only in the main database, or in backups and analytics too?
lines.ko: 한 달 안에 답해야 해요. 데이터가 메인 DB에만 있나요, 백업과 분석 시스템에도 있나요?

lines.text: Backups and the analytics warehouse as well. Backups are overwritten every ninety days.
lines.ko: 백업과 분석 웨어하우스에도요. 백업은 90일마다 덮어쓰여요.

lines.text: Then delete from live systems now, document that backups will expire, and confirm to the user in writing.
lines.ko: 그럼 운영 시스템에선 지금 지우고, 백업은 만료될 거라고 기록하고, 사용자에게 서면으로 확인해 주죠.

phrases.en: We have one month to respond.
Confirm to the user in writing.

response.situationKo: 팀에 개인정보 처리 원칙을 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why can't we just keep all the user data, in case it's useful later?

answers.text: Under data minimization, we should only keep what we need for a clear purpose.
Every extra record is a liability. If we're breached, we're responsible for all of it.
Legally, 'it might be useful' isn't a valid reason to store personal data.
Because the data you don't have can't leak. Simple as that.

title: Sprint retrospective
settingKo: 개발팀이 2주 스프린트를 돌아보며 개선점을 찾습니다.

lines.text: What went well this sprint, and what should we change?
lines.ko: 이번 스프린트에서 잘된 점과 바꿀 점이 뭐예요?

lines.text: Pairing on the payment bug was great, but we kept getting pulled into unplanned support requests.
lines.ko: 결제 버그를 짝 프로그래밍한 건 좋았는데 계획에 없던 지원 요청에 계속 끌려갔어요.

lines.text: How much time did those interruptions cost us, roughly?
lines.ko: 그 방해로 대략 얼마나 시간을 잃었어요?

lines.text: About a third of the sprint. Maybe we rotate one person each week to handle support so the rest can focus.
lines.ko: 스프린트의 3분의 1쯤이요. 매주 한 명씩 돌아가며 지원을 맡고 나머지는 집중하면 어떨까요?

options: 매주 한 명이 돌아가며 지원 담당

phrases.en: We kept getting pulled into support requests.

response.situationKo: 회고 회의에서 잘된 점과 개선점을 균형 있게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Your turn. Keep, stop, or start?

answers.text: Keep the daily demos. Stop merging on Friday afternoons. Start writing tests before fixes.
The design handoff worked well. Next sprint, I'd like us to agree on scope before day one.
I'd like us to stop scheduling meetings during focus hours in the morning.
Keep the snacks, stop the surprise deadlines, start shorter stand-ups.

title: Is the model good enough?
settingKo: 데이터 과학자들이 새 AI 모델의 출시 여부를 논의합니다.

lines.text: The new model scores ninety-four percent accuracy on our test set, up from eighty-nine.
lines.ko: 새 모델이 테스트 세트에서 정확도 94퍼센트로 89에서 올랐어요.

lines.text: Impressive, but how does it do on the rare cases? Accuracy can hide poor performance on small groups.
lines.ko: 인상적이네요. 그런데 드문 사례에선요? 정확도는 소수 집단에서의 낮은 성능을 가릴 수 있어요.

lines.text: Fair point. On non-English inputs, it's actually slightly worse than the old model.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 영어가 아닌 입력에선 사실 예전 모델보다 조금 못해요.

lines.text: Then we shouldn't ship it globally yet. Let's launch for English first and fix the multilingual gap.
lines.ko: 그럼 아직 전 세계 출시는 안 돼요. 영어부터 출시하고 다국어 격차를 고치죠.

phrases.en: Accuracy can hide poor performance on small groups.
phrases.ko: 정확도는 소수 집단의 낮은 성능을 가릴 수 있어요.

response.situationKo: 모델 성능 지표에 대해 비판적으로 질문해 보세요.
response.prompt: The model's overall accuracy is ninety-five percent. Ready to ship?

answers.text: How does it perform broken down by language and user group?
What's the false positive rate? In our case, that's the costly mistake.
Compared to what baseline? Ninety-five sounds good until you know the old number.
Before we ship, can we test it on last month's real edge cases?

title: Lab safety briefing
settingKo: 새로 온 연구원에게 실험실 안전 규칙을 설명합니다.

lines.text: Goggles and a lab coat at all times, even if you're only walking through to the office.
lines.ko: 사무실로 지나가기만 해도 보안경과 실험복은 항상 착용해요.

lines.text: Anything volatile goes in the fume hood, and never work alone here after six p.m.
lines.ko: 휘발성 물질은 흄 후드 안에서만, 그리고 오후 6시 이후엔 여기서 절대 혼자 작업하지 마세요.

lines.text: What should I do if something spills on my skin?
lines.ko: 피부에 뭐가 묻으면 어떻게 해야 하나요?

lines.text: Go straight to the emergency shower by the door and rinse for fifteen minutes. Then report it, however small.
lines.ko: 문 옆 비상 샤워기로 바로 가서 15분간 씻어 내요. 그리고 아무리 작아도 보고하세요.

phrases.en: Never work alone here after six.

response.situationKo: 새 동료에게 작업장의 안전 수칙 하나를 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Anything I need to know before I start?

answers.text: Always label every container with the contents and the date. Unlabeled bottles get thrown out.
Make sure you know where the fire extinguisher and first aid kit are before anything else.
answers.noteKo: 가장 먼저 할 일을 알려 줘요.

answers.text: Never eat or drink in here, not even water.
If you're unsure about anything, stop and ask. Nobody minds, honestly.

title: Responding to reviewers
settingKo: 공동 저자들이 논문 심사위원의 지적에 어떻게 답할지 논의합니다.

lines.text: Reviewer two says our sample is too homogeneous to support the general claims in the abstract.
lines.ko: 심사위원 2는 표본이 너무 동질적이라 초록의 일반화된 주장을 뒷받침하지 못한대요.

lines.text: Annoyingly, they have a point. Can we soften the abstract rather than collect new data?
lines.ko: 짜증 나지만 일리가 있어요. 새 데이터를 모으는 대신 초록 표현을 완화할 수 있을까요?

lines.text: I think so. We'll limit the claim to the population we studied and add it to the limitations section.
lines.ko: 그럴 것 같아요. 연구한 집단으로 주장을 한정하고 한계 부분에 추가하죠.

lines.text: And in the response letter, let's thank them and quote the revised sentence directly.
lines.ko: 그리고 답변서에서 감사를 표하고 수정한 문장을 그대로 인용하죠.

options: 주장을 연구 집단으로 한정하고 한계에 추가

phrases.en: Add it to the limitations section.

response.situationKo: 심사위원의 비판에 정중하게 답하는 문장을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Reviewer: The authors have not considered alternative explanations.

answers.text: We thank the reviewer for this point. We have now added a paragraph discussing two alternative explanations.
We agree this was missing. In the revised manuscript, see section four point two.
We appreciate the comment; however, the alternative suggested is ruled out by the control experiment in Figure three.
Fair critique. We've expanded the discussion accordingly.

title: Designing a clinical trial
settingKo: 연구팀이 새 치료법의 임상시험 설계를 논의합니다.

lines.text: If we don't randomize, the patients who choose the new treatment may simply be healthier to begin with.
lines.ko: 무작위 배정을 안 하면 새 치료를 선택한 환자가 애초에 더 건강할 수 있어요.

lines.text: Agreed. And it should be double-blind, so neither patients nor doctors know who's receiving what.
lines.ko: 동의해요. 그리고 이중맹검이어야 해요. 환자도 의사도 누가 뭘 받는지 모르게요.

lines.text: What's our primary endpoint? We need to commit to it before we see any results.
lines.ko: 1차 평가 변수는 뭐로 하죠? 결과를 보기 전에 정해 둬야 해요.

lines.text: Hospital readmission within ninety days. It's objective and matters to patients.
lines.ko: 90일 내 재입원이요. 객관적이고 환자에게 중요하니까요.

phrases.en: Commit to it before we see any results.

response.situationKo: 연구 설계의 약점을 지적하고 개선안을 제시해 보세요.
response.prompt: We'll compare people who use the app with people who don't. Any concerns?

answers.text: There's a risk of selection bias. People who choose the app may already be more motivated.
I'd suggest randomizing who gets access, even if it's only a pilot group.
We should at least control for age, income, and baseline health, which are obvious confounders.
Honestly, without a proper control group, we won't know if the app did anything.

title: Questions after a talk
settingKo: 학회 발표 후 청중의 질문에 답합니다.

lines.text: Thanks for the talk. How would your method handle noisy sensor data from cheaper devices?
lines.ko: 발표 감사합니다. 저렴한 기기의 노이즈 많은 센서 데이터는 그 방법으로 어떻게 처리하나요?

lines.text: That's a great question, and honestly, it's our biggest open problem.
lines.ko: 좋은 질문이고, 솔직히 저희의 가장 큰 미해결 과제예요.

lines.text: In early tests, accuracy dropped by about fifteen percent, so we're exploring a filtering step before the model.
lines.ko: 초기 테스트에서 정확도가 약 15퍼센트 떨어져서 모델 앞에 필터링 단계를 두는 걸 검토 중이에요.

lines.text: Interesting. I'd be happy to share a dataset we collected with low-cost sensors, if that helps.
lines.ko: 흥미롭네요. 도움이 된다면 저희가 저가 센서로 모은 데이터셋을 공유할게요.

response.situationKo: 발표 후 답하기 어려운 질문을 받았습니다. 솔직하고 전문적으로 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Have you tested this outside the lab, in real-world conditions?

answers.text: Not yet, and that's a fair question. Our next step is a three-month field trial with a partner hospital.
Only in a limited pilot. I'd expect some loss of performance, which is why we're cautious about the claims.
Honestly, no, and I think that's the most important gap in this work.
Partially. Happy to chat after the session about what we saw.

title: Supply chain delays
settingKo: 운영팀이 부품 공급 지연에 대한 대책을 세웁니다.

lines.text: Our main chip supplier just pushed delivery back by eight weeks because of a factory fire.
lines.ko: 주요 칩 공급 업체가 공장 화재로 납품을 8주 미뤘어요.

lines.text: How much inventory do we have on hand, and how fast are we burning through it?
lines.ko: 현재 재고가 얼마나 있고, 얼마나 빨리 소진되고 있어요?

lines.text: About five weeks at the current production rate, so we're three weeks short.
lines.ko: 현재 생산 속도로 5주쯤이라 3주가 모자라요.

lines.text: Let's qualify the backup supplier immediately and prioritize production for our highest-margin products.
lines.ko: 예비 공급 업체 승인을 즉시 진행하고 마진이 가장 높은 제품부터 생산하죠.

phrases.en: How fast are we burning through it?

response.situationKo: 공급 문제를 고객에게 알리고 대안을 제시해 보세요.
response.prompt: Will my order still arrive by the end of the month?

answers.text: Unfortunately, we now expect a two-week delay. In the meantime, we can ship half the order on time.
We can offer an equivalent model that's in stock, at the same price.
Your order has priority, and I'll update you every Monday until it ships.
I won't sugarcoat it: it'll be late. But here's how we can soften the impact.

title: Evaluating vendor proposals
settingKo: 구매팀이 소프트웨어 업체 제안서를 비교 평가합니다.

lines.text: Vendor A is cheapest, but their proposal is vague about support response times.
lines.ko: A 업체가 가장 싸지만 제안서에 지원 응답 시간이 모호해요.

lines.text: Vendor B is twenty percent more expensive but guarantees a four-hour response, with penalties if they miss it.
lines.ko: B 업체는 20퍼센트 비싸지만 4시간 응답을 보장하고 못 지키면 위약금이 있어요.

lines.text: Given that this system runs our warehouse, downtime would cost far more than the price difference.
lines.ko: 이 시스템이 창고를 돌리니까 중단되면 가격 차이보다 훨씬 큰 손실이 나요.

lines.text: Agreed. Let's go back to Vendor A and ask them to match B's service levels before we decide.
lines.ko: 동의해요. 결정 전에 A 업체에 B 수준의 서비스를 맞춰 달라고 다시 요청해 보죠.

phrases.en: With penalties if they miss it.

response.situationKo: 업체 선정 회의에서 가격이 아닌 기준을 강조해 의견을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why not just go with the cheapest option?

answers.text: Because the total cost over three years, including support and training, is actually higher.
Their reliability record is weak, and switching vendors later would be expensive and disruptive.
Cheap now often means hidden costs later, like custom integration work.
We've been burned by cheapest-wins before. Remember the old payroll system?
answers.noteKo: be burned는 데어 본 적 있다예요.

title: Stuck in customs
settingKo: 수출 화물이 세관에 묶여 물류 대행사와 통화합니다.

lines.text: Your shipment is being held because the commercial invoice doesn't match the packing list.
lines.ko: 상업 송장과 포장 명세서가 일치하지 않아서 화물이 보류됐어요.

lines.text: What exactly is the discrepancy?
lines.ko: 정확히 어떤 불일치예요?

lines.text: The invoice says four hundred units, but the packing list shows four hundred and twenty.
lines.ko: 송장엔 400개인데 포장 명세서엔 420개로 돼 있어요.

lines.text: The extra twenty are free samples. I'll send a corrected invoice listing them at zero value within the hour.
lines.ko: 추가 20개는 무료 샘플이에요. 한 시간 안에 그걸 0원으로 기재한 수정 송장을 보낼게요.

response.situationKo: 물류 대행사에게 지연된 화물의 상황과 해결 일정을 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Hi, this is about your shipment number four-four-seven.

answers.text: Thanks for calling. What's the status, and what documents do you need from us?
Is there any way to expedite clearance? The customer needs it by Friday.
How long is it likely to be held, and are there storage fees in the meantime?
Uh-oh. What's gone wrong, and what's the estimated release date?

title: An HR investigation
settingKo: 인사 담당자가 직장 내 괴롭힘 신고에 대해 증인을 면담합니다.

lines.text: This conversation is confidential. We're speaking to several people, and no conclusions have been reached.
lines.ko: 이 대화는 기밀입니다. 여러 분과 이야기하고 있고 아직 결론은 나지 않았어요.

lines.text: Understood. I'll tell you what I saw, but I don't want this to come back on me.
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 본 대로 말할게요. 다만 이게 저한테 불똥이 튀진 않았으면 해요.

lines.text: Retaliation against witnesses is strictly prohibited, and we take it very seriously.
lines.ko: 증인에 대한 보복은 엄격히 금지되어 있고 저희는 아주 심각하게 다뤄요.

lines.text: In the March meeting, he shouted at her in front of the team and called her work useless.
lines.ko: 3월 회의에서 그가 팀 앞에서 그녀에게 소리치며 작업이 쓸모없다고 했어요.

phrases.en: I don't want this to come back on me.

response.situationKo: 조사에서 본 것을 사실 위주로 객관적으로 진술해 보세요.
response.prompt: In your own words, what did you witness?

answers.text: On the twelfth, I heard him say, word for word, that she should quit if she couldn't keep up.
answers.noteKo: word for word는 그대로 옮긴 말이에요.

answers.text: I saw her leave the meeting in tears, but I didn't see what happened before I arrived.
answers.noteKo: 본 것과 못 본 것을 구분해요.

answers.text: As far as I know, it's happened at least three times in team meetings.
answers.noteKo: As far as I know로 범위를 한정해요.

answers.text: I'll stick to what I saw directly, because I don't want to repeat rumors.

title: Which channel worked?
settingKo: 마케팅 분석가가 광고 채널별 성과를 해석합니다.

lines.text: According to last-click attribution, search ads drove seventy percent of sales.
lines.ko: 마지막 클릭 기준으로 보면 검색 광고가 매출의 70퍼센트를 이끌었어요.

lines.text: That model overrates search, though. People often see us on social media first, then search for us later.
lines.ko: 그 모델은 검색을 과대평가해요. 사람들은 보통 SNS에서 먼저 보고 나중에 검색하거든요.

lines.text: So cutting social might quietly reduce search conversions too?
lines.ko: 그럼 SNS를 줄이면 검색 전환도 조용히 줄어들 수 있다는 거죠?

lines.text: Exactly. Let's run a holdout test in two regions before we move any budget.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 예산을 옮기기 전에 두 지역에서 홀드아웃 테스트를 해 보죠.

response.situationKo: 데이터 해석에 의문을 제기하고 검증 방법을 제안해 보세요.
response.prompt: The data clearly shows email is our best channel. Let's double it.

answers.text: Email mostly reaches existing customers, so I'd want to see incremental sales before doubling it.
That might be correlation. Could we test sending to half the list and compare?
Before we double it, let's check whether unsubscribes rise with frequency.
Love the enthusiasm, but people who open our emails would probably buy anyway.

title: Pricing hotel rooms
settingKo: 호텔 수익 관리 담당자가 행사 기간 객실 가격을 논의합니다.

lines.text: There's a major tech conference in town next month, and occupancy for those dates is already at sixty percent.
lines.ko: 다음 달 시내에 대형 기술 콘퍼런스가 있고 그 날짜 예약률이 벌써 60퍼센트예요.

lines.text: Then we're underpriced. Competitors have raised their rates by about forty percent.
lines.ko: 그럼 우리가 너무 싸요. 경쟁사들은 요금을 약 40퍼센트 올렸어요.

lines.text: If we raise prices too quickly, we risk empty rooms if the conference is smaller than expected.
lines.ko: 너무 빨리 올리면 콘퍼런스 규모가 예상보다 작을 때 빈방이 생길 위험이 있어요.

lines.text: Let's increase gradually each week and set a minimum three-night stay for the peak days.
lines.ko: 매주 조금씩 올리고 성수기 날짜엔 최소 3박 조건을 걸죠.

response.situationKo: 가격 인상에 대한 반대 의견에 데이터로 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Won't raising prices annoy our loyal guests?

answers.text: We could protect loyalty members with a fixed rate, and raise prices only for new bookings.
Demand is well above normal, and we're still below the market rate even after the increase.
Let's exclude repeat guests and see how bookings respond for two weeks.
Fair worry. Let's send loyal guests a heads-up and a small perk.

title: The appraisal came in low
settingKo: 주택 감정가가 매매가보다 낮게 나와 중개인과 대책을 논의합니다.

lines.text: The appraisal came in at five hundred and forty thousand, which is thirty thousand below the agreed price.
lines.ko: 감정가가 54만으로 합의 가격보다 3만 낮게 나왔어요.

lines.text: Does that mean the bank won't lend us the full amount?
lines.ko: 그럼 은행이 전액을 대출해 주지 않는다는 뜻인가요?

lines.text: Right. You'd need to cover the gap in cash, renegotiate the price, or challenge the appraisal.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 차액을 현금으로 메우거나, 가격을 재협상하거나, 감정에 이의를 제기해야 해요.

lines.text: Let's challenge it first. Two similar houses on this street sold for more last month.
lines.ko: 먼저 이의를 제기하죠. 지난달 이 거리의 비슷한 집 두 채가 더 비싸게 팔렸어요.

response.situationKo: 판매자에게 감정가를 근거로 가격 재협상을 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why should we lower the price? We had a deal.

answers.text: We did, however the independent appraisal suggests the fair market value is lower.
We're still keen. Would you meet us halfway, at fifteen thousand below?
Any other buyer's bank would see the same appraisal, so it'll come up again.
answers.noteKo: 다른 구매자도 같은 문제를 겪는다는 논리예요.

answers.text: Totally understand the frustration. We're just limited by what the bank will lend.

title: Does it meet code?
settingKo: 건축가가 증축 설계를 건축 법규에 맞게 수정합니다.

lines.text: The extension looks great, but the bedroom window is too small to count as an emergency exit.
lines.ko: 증축은 멋진데 침실 창문이 비상 탈출구로 인정받기엔 너무 작아요.

lines.text: How much larger does it need to be?
lines.ko: 얼마나 더 커야 하나요?

lines.text: The opening has to be at least half a square meter, and the sill no higher than one point one meters from the floor.
lines.ko: 개구부가 최소 0.5제곱미터이고 창턱이 바닥에서 1.1미터를 넘으면 안 돼요.

lines.text: Then let's widen it and lower the sill. It'll also bring in more light, which is a bonus.
lines.ko: 그럼 넓히고 창턱을 낮추죠. 빛도 더 들어올 테니 덤이네요.

phrases.en: It doesn't count as an emergency exit.

response.situationKo: 건축가에게 설계가 법규와 예산에 맞는지 확인해 보세요.
response.prompt: Here's the final drawing. Any questions before we submit it?

answers.text: Does this comply with the new insulation rules, and will we need a separate permit for the deck?
How long does approval usually take, and when would the first inspection be?
If the council asks for changes, how much could that add to the cost?
Looks amazing. What's the most likely thing they'll push back on?

title: Insurance underwriting
settingKo: 보험 심사역이 기업 보험 가입 조건을 설명합니다.

lines.text: We can offer cover, but given the two water-damage claims last year, the premium will be higher.
lines.ko: 보험 가입은 가능하지만 작년 누수 피해 청구가 두 건이라 보험료가 높아질 거예요.

lines.text: We've since replaced all the old pipes. Would that be taken into account?
lines.ko: 그 뒤로 낡은 배관을 전부 교체했어요. 그것도 고려되나요?

lines.text: It would. If you send the contractor's invoice and an inspection report, I can reduce the excess.
lines.ko: 고려돼요. 시공 업체 청구서와 점검 보고서를 보내 주시면 자기부담금을 낮춰 드릴 수 있어요.

lines.text: Great, I'll send both today. Could you also confirm whether flood damage is covered?
lines.ko: 좋아요, 오늘 둘 다 보낼게요. 홍수 피해도 보장되는지 확인해 주실 수 있나요?

options: 배관 교체 청구서와 점검 보고서 제출

phrases.en: Would that be taken into account?

response.situationKo: 보험 약관에서 보장 범위를 꼼꼼히 확인해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you have any questions about the policy?
keywords: how do i make a claim

answers.text: What's specifically excluded, and could you confirm that in writing?
Is business interruption covered if we have to close after a fire?
What's the excess per claim, and is there an annual limit?
If something happens at two a.m., how do I make a claim, practically?

title: Can we publish this?
settingKo: 언론사 변호사가 보도 전 기사의 명예훼손 위험을 검토합니다.

lines.text: You write that the mayor took bribes. Do we have evidence of that, or just of unusual payments?
lines.ko: 시장이 뇌물을 받았다고 썼는데, 그 증거가 있어요, 아니면 이상한 지급 내역만 있어요?

lines.text: We have bank records showing payments from a contractor, and two sources who say they were for favors.
lines.ko: 시공업자로부터의 지급을 보여 주는 은행 기록과 대가성이라고 말하는 소식통 두 명이 있어요.

lines.text: Then state the payments as fact, attribute the claim about favors to the sources, and give the mayor a chance to respond.
lines.ko: 그럼 지급은 사실로 쓰고, 대가성 주장은 소식통의 말로 인용하고, 시장에게 반론 기회를 주세요.

lines.text: We've asked for comment, and we'll hold publication until tomorrow morning for their reply.
lines.ko: 논평을 요청했고 답변을 위해 내일 아침까지 보도를 보류할게요.

phrases.en: Attribute the claim to the sources.
Give them a chance to respond.

response.situationKo: 편집자로서 기자의 기사에서 법적 위험이 있는 문장을 지적해 보세요.
response.prompt: Is the article ready to go?

answers.text: Almost. This line states fraud as fact, but we only have one source. Let's attribute it.
We can't say 'stole'. 'According to court documents, funds went missing' is safer and still strong.
Did the company get a chance to respond? If not, we hold until they do.
Great story. Just soften the headline so a lawyer doesn't ruin our week.

title: What did users say?
settingKo: UX 리서처가 사용자 인터뷰 결과를 팀에 공유합니다.

lines.text: Across twelve interviews, the most common frustration was not knowing whether a payment had gone through.
lines.ko: 인터뷰 열두 건에서 가장 흔한 불만은 결제가 됐는지 알 수 없다는 거였어요.

lines.text: Interesting. Our analytics showed people abandoning checkout, but we assumed it was the price.
lines.ko: 흥미롭네요. 분석 데이터에선 결제 이탈이 보였는데 가격 때문인 줄 알았어요.

lines.text: Several people said they refreshed the page and got charged twice, so now they leave rather than risk it.
lines.ko: 몇 명은 새로고침했다가 두 번 결제돼서, 이젠 위험을 감수하느니 나간대요.

lines.text: Then a clear confirmation screen might fix more than a discount would.
lines.ko: 그럼 할인보다 명확한 확인 화면이 더 많은 걸 해결할 수도 있겠네요.

options: 결제 완료 여부를 알 수 없어서

response.situationKo: 사용자 조사 결과를 근거로 팀의 가정을 바로잡아 보세요.
response.prompt: We all agree users want more features, right?

answers.text: Actually, in the interviews, most people asked for fewer steps, not more features.
The data suggests they barely use half of what we have. Simpler might win.
What they asked for most was reliability. Several people mentioned crashes unprompted.
Not quite! They mostly want the existing stuff to work better.
